stories.headline: Bank of Canada holds rate at 2.25% for fourth consecutive time, warns of possible hikes if oil shock persists
stories.summary: The Bank of Canada kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 2.25% on April 29 for the fourth consecutive meeting, citing twin uncertainties — rising oil prices from the Iran war and the upcoming CUSMA review — that could push the rate either higher or lower. Governor Tiff Macklem flagged that consecutive hikes were possible if the oil shock proved persistent, while also signalling encouragement at federal efforts to diversify the economy.

stories.headline: CSIS annual report flags Khalistani extremist threat and names India, China as top foreign interference actors
stories.summary: Canada's spy agency CSIS released its 2025 Public Report on April 30, tabling it in Parliament, which for the first time formally used the term 'Canada-based Khalistani extremist' (CBKE) and named India, China, Russia, Iran and Pakistan as the main perpetrators of foreign interference. The report drew extensive coverage across Indian and Canadian media, with CSIS noting no CBKE-linked attacks occurred in Canada in 2025 but that the threat remained ongoing.

stories.headline: Carney attends EPC summit in Armenia as first non-European nation; conducts bilateral meetings with European leaders
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney travelled to Yerevan, Armenia on May 2-3 to attend the European Political Community summit, becoming the first non-European country to participate in the 48-plus nation grouping. He held bilateral meetings with Armenian PM Nikol Pashinyan, Polish PM Donald Tusk, and European Parliament President Roberta Metsola, framing the visit around Ukraine defence support and deepening trade and investment ties with Europe amid U.S. tariff pressures.

stories.headline: Carney rejects using energy as U.S. trade leverage; Poilievre demands answers on pipeline and negotiating position
stories.summary: In his first sit-down interview with The Canadian Press since becoming PM, Carney said Canada would not use energy or critical minerals as 'leverage' in upcoming CUSMA negotiations, while saying a new Alberta pipeline is 'more likely than not.' Conservative leader Poilievre responded with sustained criticism — saying Carney has 'wasted an entire year' on the pipeline, should disclose Canada's actual bargaining chips, and that only the government should negotiate with the U.S. after Conservative MPs visited Washington.

stories.headline: Carney spring economic update shows $66.9B deficit; Liberals and Conservatives clash on fiscal record
stories.summary: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne tabled Canada's spring economic update on April 28, projecting a $66.9 billion deficit for 2025-26 — down from a prior $78.3 billion forecast but up sharply from pre-pandemic baselines. The update included billions for skilled trades training and a fuel excise tax pause. Poilievre accused Carney of 'doubling the deficit,' while Bloc Québécois called the document insufficient, and the NDP faulted it for abandoning pharmacare.

stories.headline: Carney launches Canada's first sovereign wealth fund at $25B; airport privatization linked
stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney announced the 'Canada Strong Fund,' a $25 billion sovereign wealth fund open to direct Canadian investment, to finance major infrastructure projects in energy, mining, agriculture and technology. Linked coverage noted the government is also consulting on privatizing airport authorities, with the fund serving as partial rationale. Opposition parties including the Bloc and Conservatives raised transparency concerns and criticized the fund's opacity.

stories.headline: Liberal majority formalizes control of parliamentary committees; opposition accuses government of using new powers to limit debate
stories.summary: After three byelection wins and five floor crossings gave the Liberals a 174-seat majority, the government moved immediately on April 27 to restructure House committees — adding two Liberal seats per committee. Opposition MPs accused the Liberals of using the majority to go in camera at committees and block access to documents on a $6.6 billion IT project (Cúram software). The Conservatives also accused the government of attempting to poach Conservative MP Kelly DeRidder.

stories.headline: Canada selected as host country for new multinational Defence Security and Resilience Bank
stories.summary: Canada was confirmed on April 29-30 as the host country for a new multinational defence bank designed to provide long-term, low-cost financing for NATO members and allies rearmament. The bank's founding charter was agreed in Montreal after two rounds of negotiations; Canadian cities including Toronto, Ottawa, Vancouver and Montreal are competing to host the bank's headquarters. Some European countries including Britain and Germany had previously raised questions about the initiative.

stories.headline: Polling shows Liberals hold commanding lead; Poilievre faces leadership pressure amid negative personal ratings
stories.summary: Multiple polling firms released data in late April and early May showing the Liberal Party leading the Conservatives by approximately 11-14 points nationally (Liberals ~44-48%, Conservatives ~34-37%). Separate Angus Reid polling showed a majority of Canadians believe Poilievre should be replaced as Conservative leader, including 30% of Conservative supporters, with two-thirds of women holding a negative view of him.
